assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Kiyotaki-Moore mechanism, in which collateral values and credit constraints amplify and propagate shocks, is foundational for macro-finance. It underlies much post-2008 analysis of credit cycles, balance-sheet channels and financial frictions. It changed how macroeconomists model financial amplification, and its value does not depend on one field's taste.
assessment.attribution: The core contribution is the 1997 Kiyotaki-Moore paper, which makes the two-person attribution clean. Gertler and Gilchrist are important for the financial accelerator and its empirical side, but they build on and extend the framework. Bernanke's earlier recognition also complicates a broader group. I propose the two originators.
assessment.maturity: Nearly three decades of theory, quantitative and empirical work confirm the idea. It is well established and its influence is documented.
uncertainties: Committee tastes on whether the financial-frictions theme is already adequately recognised after the 2022 prize.
Whether the Gertler-Gilchrist-Bernanke accelerator strand should share credit.
My recall of citation and policy-use evidence is not verified against sources.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection reshaped international trade theory and empirics. Exporter productivity premia, the extensive margin and new gains-from-trade channels are now standard. The work moved the field from industry-level to firm-level analysis and informed policy analysis.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the central model. Helpman contributed the broader new trade theory with firms, including the proximity-concentration and heterogeneous-firm FDI work. Redding has important quantitative and spatial extensions, but is later and more derivative. Bernard, Eaton and Kortum are important adjacent contributors who are not on this ballot's credited names.
assessment.maturity: More than twenty years of replication and extension. The framework is widely adopted and well tested.
uncertainties: Overlap with the trade prize recognition of Krugman, and with the Eaton-Kortum or Bernard et al. strands that are not credited here.
Whether the committee sees the contribution as a model refinement or a paradigm shift.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The work built the modern formal framework for political economics, covering electoral rules, constitutions, fiscal outcomes and state capacity. It also links well to empirical comparative politics. It established a field that connects institutions with economic policy outcomes, and its influence reaches across economics and political science.
assessment.attribution: Persson-Tabellini (the 2000 book and associated papers) and Besley (state capacity, accountability and the political economy of development) are the clear core trio. Acemoglu and Robinson, who share some themes, were recognised in 2024. Distinct credit exists for each of these three.
assessment.maturity: Developed over thirty years with extensive empirical testing, including on electoral rules and state capacity. Field-defining.
uncertainties: Conflict disclosure: I have co-authored with Persson (on corruption as a collective-action problem), and the profile also lists a Stockholm affiliation proximity. I disclose this and do not adjudicate it.
Thematic overlap with the 2024 institutions prize might be seen as reducing novelty.
Empirical identification of some constitutional effects remains debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Structural estimation of differentiated-product demand (BLP) and of dynamic industry models (Ericson-Pakes, with Olley-Pakes on production) turned industrial organisation into a quantitative discipline. It is used in merger review, antitrust and regulation as well as academic research, and has a large reach beyond IO.
assessment.attribution: The BLP trio of Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes has a clear credit structure, and Pakes also led the dynamic and production-function strands. Bresnahan, Reiss and Levin contributed adjacent empirical IO work but are less central to this particular innovation.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of use confirm it, with applications in policy practice.
uncertainties: Whether Pakes alone or the BLP trio best reflects credit.
Concerns about the identifying assumptions and computational fragility of structural methods.
Competition from other empirical methods candidates for committee attention.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The China-shock research documented the local labour-market effects of import competition and, with the task-based framework, shaped the debate on technology, trade and wage inequality. It changed both academic and public understanding of adjustment costs. It combines credible quasi-experimental identification with large policy relevance.
assessment.attribution: The ADH papers (Autor-Dorn-Hanson) are the core of the trade-shock strand. Autor and Katz have the long-standing task and skill-biased technical change work, in which Acemoglu is also central. Dividing credit between the trade and technology strands is difficult.
assessment.maturity: The core papers date to 2013 and after. The results are widely replicated and challenged, so the debate is still active and long-run assessment is incomplete.
uncertainties: Ongoing debate about magnitudes and the shift-share identification strategy.
Ambiguity over how credit divides between the task-framework and trade-shock strands.
A relatively recent contribution compared with some other candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population administrative data used to measure intergenerational mobility and the effects of neighbourhoods transformed empirical public and labour economics. It changed the data standards of the field and informed policy debate. The work is high impact, and its value rests on new measurement and new facts about opportunity.
assessment.attribution: Chetty is the clear leader of the programme, with Hendren central to the causal neighbourhood-effects work and Friedman to the large-scale data projects. A team structure makes tight attribution hard, and it is not obvious how many people the committee would credit.
assessment.maturity: Dates mostly from the 2014 onward period, so it is comparatively recent. Replications and follow-up studies are accumulating, but long-run outcomes of the policy ideas remain to be seen.
uncertainties: Maturity is shorter than for several higher-ranked candidates.
Some methodological criticism of the neighbourhood-effect and mobility-measurement estimates.
The choice between a narrow and a wide laureate set.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The alternating-offers bargaining model (1982) is a canonical result. Rubinstein-Wolinsky bargaining in markets connected bargaining theory to decentralised trade and search. It is foundational across microeconomic theory, labour and industrial organisation, and underlies applied models.
assessment.attribution: Rubinstein is the principal originator of the alternating-offers solution. Wolinsky's market bargaining adds a distinct strand. Binmore contributed to the strategic foundation of the Nash programme and to the follow-up, but Stahl's earlier related work is outside the list, which adds attribution complexity.
assessment.maturity: More than forty years of confirmation and use. Fully mature.
uncertainties: The game theory area has received several prizes, which may affect the committee's view of balance.
Whether Rubinstein alone or the pair is better, given the Stahl precedent.
Some members could regard the contribution as already absorbed into standard theory rather than newly pending.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Hsieh-Klenow (2009) quantified how misallocation of inputs across firms can explain large cross-country TFP gaps. It gave growth and development economics a concrete measurement framework and stimulated a large literature on distortions, firm dynamics and policy reform. Its main strength is the combination of simple theory with micro-data measurement.
assessment.attribution: The central paper and its follow-ups have a clear Hsieh-Klenow core. Restuccia and Rogerson's related work on policy distortions and misallocation is important but not credited here, and the credited name Restuccia would have to be weighed against Hsieh and Klenow if the committee prefers a wider group. I propose the two with the most direct claim.
assessment.maturity: About seventeen years of application, though measurement debates over the interpretation of dispersion in marginal products persist.
uncertainties: Criticism that measured dispersion partly reflects measurement error and adjustment frictions.
Credit allocation relative to Restuccia and Rogerson.
How the committee weighs a measurement framework against more causal evidence.
